title: The Lora Lemma
description: This paper challenges the prevailing assumption that Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) in language models constitutes meaningful learning. It demonstrates that LoRA operates within the latent constraints of the pre-trained model and thus cannot introduce epistemically novel capacity. Using the case of SEAL (Self-Edit for Assimilation of Language), we show how reinforcement learning is used to reinforce priors rather than extend them. We argue that LoRA-based claims of adaptation constitute a category error: mistaking internal reconfiguration for learning. The implications extend beyond LoRA and touch on the broader misuse of mathematical perturbations as proxies for knowledge incorporation.
